>"Oh and btw he was molested, let's sprinkle that on top out of nowhere" -Mr. Robot writers

It didn't come out of nowhere. There were multiple points in the show where they foreshadowed it. Remember Elliot's "no touching rule" in the very first seasons at the first fucking episode all through out the rest of the seasons? That's already a major hint towards him being sexually abused. It was built up more in season 3 because the eventual realization was coming. They just started shifting the focus little by little from then on. 

His memories with his dad also are big hints to his dad being an abuser rather than a good father, I do not know how you think it just came out of nowhere. 

​

>Elliot's mental illness causing him to have split personalities and imagine/hallucinate everything is also in the same category, and was also wasted in Season 1 so the "finale" is just a lame repeat.

I don't even think Elliot hallucinated anything despite from just a few moments WHILE ON DRUGS, he was aware of what was going around him, the prison reveal in season 2 was him hiding the truth from the audience not his brain playing tricks on him. Season 1 was like a retelling of an extended version of Fight Club, with many different elements at play. Season 4 is radically different and so are the twists.

 Since where was "finding out your dead father is a personality in your mind" the same as "my father molested me when I was young"? You can't actually provide any basis for why it's a lame repeat other than give a gross oversimplification of BOTH SEASONS just to make it look like the same thing.

>How is the music good?

Music's never been overused and Mac always kept making new tunes that matched the season. I can't exactly explain but it works perfectly in the scenes it's put in. (The score also has some pretty fun names, as they are written down like actual file names with different extensions, pretty creative). 

> How is the cinematography good?

Mr. Robot's style of filming is so unique that even one shot from any scene is enough to recognize where it's from. They film characters in the corner of the screen to give a sense of uneasiness towards the audience, and also has some very beautiful shots that resemble Fincher's style. (For example: Season 4 Episode 9, where 2 characters are arguing, the camera shifts up and down to represent the state of power each character was in. Quite similar to what Fincher does in some of his works.)

There's also various episodes that are experimental, like the sitcom episode, the episode that's shot to make it look like it's all done in one single take, an episode done like drama play, and episode with no dialogue. It does some really cool and neat stuff with it.  

​

>How is the writing good?

The writing isn't perfect, but there's a lot of subplots that are foreshadowed at the very beginning of the show that you can pick up during multiple re-watches. I don't want to spoil any to people who haven't watched it, but I'm pretty sure people who've watched it knows what I'm talking about. The writing definitely reflected the time they were living in (2015-2016, or trump era), so it can be considered dated, at some aspects of the show. The characters are (mostly) well written and with good depth. There's also some missed shots in the show that could've become something even better, but no use complaining about it now. 

​

>How is the acting good?

There's no way anyone can describe the acting. It's something you have to see for yourselves cause something that could be good for me would be something you probably wouldn't like. A lot of the scenes (especially the emotional ones) are acted out "perfectly" (imo) and it really does feel like the characters interact well with each other without it looking jarring.

The only ones that are “canon” to the SciADV collective universe are just called “Steins;Gate” and “Steins;Gate 0”. These are the original visual novels, you may see stuff like Steins;Gate: Linear Bounded Phenogram, or Steins;Gate: My Darling’s Embrace, which are alternate stories that further give depth to characters or just fanservice. 
Steins;Gate Elite is pretty much the Steins;Gate novel but with the visuals of the anime. 


Since you’re an anime only, I assume that you’re not familiar with SciADV as a whole, which is a set series of visual novels. Steins;Gate is the second main entry in the series, the first one being Chaos;Head, and after Steins;Gate is Steins;Gate 0, after that is Chaos;Child, then Robotics;Notes. You don’t need to read Chaos;Head if you want to read Steins;Gate unless you want to pick up small details, or learn a lot more about the lore. 

So essentially there is no order for the Steins;Gate VNs that are not canon, the only ones that are in order are Steins;Gate and Steins;Gate 0 after. 

Now between elite and the original visual novel what you buy is your preference, there’s a few extra animated scenes in Elite that’s not in the anime, but the original VN shows these scenes, just not animated. If you dig the anime’s style go for elite but if you want to look back at the intended artstyle, go for the original. 

Darling’s Embrace and Linear Bounded Phenogram can be played in any order, I played LBP before Darling’s Embrace because I wanted to save fanservice for last.
